verdict.summary: Lever OAuth is only available through its partner integration program: you apply, wait for Lever's partnerships team to approve you and issue a sandbox, and Lever itself creates your OAuth client. Production credentials come only after you submit a help-center article, sandbox logins, support info and pass a live QA walkthrough with Lever.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: There is no self-serve app console. You need partnership approval, then a sandbox account, then Lever creates the sandbox OAuth app from your form. Lever gives no timeframe for any of these; the range is our estimate.

timeToProd.assumes: A partner integration reading candidate/opportunity data for any Lever customer; there is no faster OAuth path (customer API keys are for internal use only).
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partnership approval, Lever creating sandbox and production OAuth apps, scheduling the QA runthrough meeting, and Lever confirming the production switch.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The four-step process is sourced; Lever states no review timings, so the total is an estimate.

prerequisites.item: Approved Lever partnership (apply via the Become a Partner form)
prerequisites.why: Lever says OAuth is part of its partner integration program and apps must be registered; the sandbox is issued only once you're approved.

prerequisites.item: A product that integrates with recruiting workflows
prerequisites.why: The interest form asks how your product integrates with recruiting workflows, and the partnerships team 'evaluates alignment and fit'.

prerequisites.item: A square logo at a direct URL (150x150px recommended) and a 20–140 character description
prerequisites.why: Required fields on the OAuth registration form; the description shows in Lever's integration ecosystem.

prerequisites.item: A public help-center article describing setup and use
prerequisites.why: One of the four items required to move to production.

scopeTiers.tier: Read scopes for core recruiting data
scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent that summarizes pipelines and candidates. Every scope sits behind the same partner process; there is no lighter tier. Lever suggests most use cases need 5–8 scopes, max 20.
write:admin includes the matching read:admin permissions, so registering both is redundant. Functional concerns may come up in the QA runthrough.
Requisitions endpoints work only for customers with Lever TRM Enterprise or the Advanced HR feature, so they fail for some connected customers.

steps.title: Apply to the Lever partner program
steps.detail: Submit the Become a Partner interest form describing your product and how it integrates with recruiting workflows.

steps.title: Wait for partnership approval and a sandbox account
steps.detail: Lever's partnerships team reviews 'alignment and fit', then provisions a Lever sandbox. Sandbox email is disabled, so sign in via the login link rather than invite emails.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: No timeframe is published; the duration is our guess.

steps.title: Draft the OAuth registration
steps.detail: Prepare name, 20–140 char description, callback URI(s) (http allowed in sandbox; extra callbacks beyond the first go through support), direct square logo URL, and a least-privilege scope list (5–8 typical, 20 max).

steps.title: Submit the sandbox OAuth registration form
steps.detail: Sign in to the sandbox and submit the form under Settings > Integrations. Keep a copy of what you submitted for debugging.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The URL returned 302 to hire.sandbox.lever.co/auth/login on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Wait for Lever to create the sandbox client
steps.detail: Lever creates the OAuth app and sends a Client ID and Secret.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow against sandbox
steps.detail: Authorize at https://sandbox-lever.auth0.com/authorize with response_type=code, state, scope (space-separated, include offline_access) and audience=https://api.sandbox.lever.co/v1/; exchange at the matching /oauth/token; call https://api.sandbox.lever.co/v1/. Lever's integrator-resources repo has an example app and Postman collection.

steps.title: Write the help-center article and support info
steps.detail: Draft a plain-language article (how to enable, screenshot of requested scopes, how to use, what it looks like in Lever) and the technical support form answers.

steps.title: Create sandbox logins for Lever and submit for production
steps.detail: Add sadmin@levertest.com and integration-support@lever.co to your sandbox, capture screenshots, supply ecosystem listing info, and send everything to Lever integration support.

steps.title: QA runthrough meeting with Lever
steps.detail: Share your screen and connect/use the integration as a customer would. Make any requested changes; Lever re-verifies in your sandbox.

steps.title: Receive production credentials
steps.detail: Lever issues a separate production OAuth app. Production can have a different configuration than sandbox.

steps.title: Switch to production and confirm go-live
steps.detail: Point auth at https://auth.lever.co (audience https://api.lever.co/v1/) and API calls at https://api.lever.co/v1/, then confirm with Lever so the ecosystem listing moves from 'coming soon' to available.

agentCanDo: Draft the partner application and the OAuth registration fields
Pick a least-privilege scope list (write:admin implies read:admin)
Implement the auth-code flow with audience, state and refresh-token rotation
Write the help-center article and support form answers
Add backoff for 429s around the 10 rps steady limit
humanMustDo: Apply to the partner program and talk to Lever's partnerships team
Sign in to the sandbox and submit the registration form
Add Lever's two test logins to the sandbox
Run the live QA walkthrough with Lever
Customer side: a Lever Super Admin authorizes the integration

blockers.symptom: Auth page shows 'Oops!, something went wrong' with 'invalid_request : Unknown client'
blockers.cause: Client ID not registered on that auth server (for example, a sandbox client used against auth.lever.co).
blockers.fix: Use https://sandbox-lever.auth0.com for sandbox clients and auth.lever.co only for production credentials.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: auth.lever.co/authorize with client_id=x returned HTTP 400 with 'invalid_request : Unknown client: x' on 2026-10-20. Lever's docs list the related '403 ClientID not found' for the wrong auth URL.

blockers.fix: Add audience=https://api.lever.co/v1/ (sandbox: https://api.sandbox.lever.co/v1/), with the trailing slash.

blockers.symptom: 403 'The key you provided does not have access to this endpoint'
blockers.cause: Scope missing from the authorize request or not registered on the auth server.
blockers.fix: Request the scope in the redirect and ask Lever to add it to your registered app.

blockers.symptom: 403 'Unable to find a signing key that matches'
blockers.cause: Sandbox token sent to the production API, or vice versa.
blockers.fix: Pair sandbox tokens with api.sandbox.lever.co and production tokens with api.lever.co.

blockers.symptom: Redirect lands on a URL containing 'undefined'
blockers.cause: Redirect parameters don't match your registration; callbacks can't vary per customer.
blockers.fix: Use exactly a registered callback URI; request extra callbacks via support.

blockers.symptom: No sandbox access or invite emails never arrive
blockers.cause: Sandbox is only issued after partner approval, and sandbox email is disabled.
blockers.fix: Get approved first; sign in via the login link instead of waiting for email.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 1 hour by default; refresh tokens (requested with offline_access) expire after one year or 90 days of inactivity, and each refresh returns a new refresh token.
Rate limit defaults to 10 requests/second steady with bursts to 20, per key; Lever says the defaults aren't guaranteed and recommends exponential backoff.
Authorization is org-wide: a Lever Super Admin connects the integration for the whole account and can revoke it in settings.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs don't say whether other admin roles can authorize.

nuances.text: Sandbox and production are separate OAuth apps with separate auth servers (sandbox-lever.auth0.com vs auth.lever.co); EU customers are redirected to the right data center automatically.
API keys (Basic Auth) are for customers' internal workflows and need the Data API feature; partner integrations are expected to use OAuth.
Lever keeps using the sandbox logins you give it to check your integration for disruptions after launch, so don't delete them.
